'''Johnny Lee O'Bryant III''' (born June 1, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Anyang Jung Kwan Jang Red Boosters]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]].<ref>{{cite web|title=#2 Johnny O'Bryant III|url=http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205158650|work=lsusports.net|access-date=June 15, 2014|archive-date=July 14, 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140714175714/http://www.lsusports.net/ViewArticle.dbml?ATCLID=205158650|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==High school career==
Considered a four-star recruit by [[ESPN.com]], O'Bryant was listed as the No. 7 power forward and the No. 46 player in the nation in 2011.<ref>{{cite web|title=Johnny O'Bryant Recruiting Profile|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/58503/johnny-obryant|work=ESPN.com|access-date=July 27, 2015}}</ref>

==College career==
In his three-year college career at [[LSU Tigers basketball|Louisiana State University]], O'Bryant was one of just 14 LSU players to record 1,000 career points and 700 career rebounds. He was also a two-time first-team All-SEC honoree.<ref name=espn>{{cite web|title=Johnny O'Bryant III leaving for NBA|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/draft2014/story/_/id/10710828/johnny-obryant-iii-lsu-tigers-enter-nba-draft|work=ESPN.com|date=April 1, 2014|access-date=June 15, 2014}}</ref>

On April 1, 2014, he declared for the NBA draft, foregoing his final year of college eligibility.<ref name="espn" />

==Professional career==
===Milwaukee Bucks (2014–2016)===
On June 26, 2014, O'Bryant was selected with the 36th overall pick in the [[2014 NBA draft]] by the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2014/06/26/bucks-take-obryant-in-2nd-round-of-nba-draft/11444591/ | title=Bucks take O'Bryant in 2nd round of NBA draft | work=USAToday.com | date=June 26, 2014 | access-date=June 27, 2014}}</ref> On July 30, 2014, he signed with the Bucks after averaging 8.2 points in five [[2014 NBA Summer League|Summer League]] games for the team.<ref>{{cite news|title=Bucks Sign Second Round Pick Johnny O'Bryant|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/bucks-sign-second-round-pick-johnny-obryant|access-date=July 30, 2014|work=NBA.com|date=July 30, 2014}}</ref> On October 9, he suffered a grade III sprain of the medial collateral ligament (MCL) in his right knee.<ref>{{cite news|title=INJURY UPDATE ON JOHNNY O'BRYANT|url=http://www.nba.com/bucks/release/injury-update-johnny-obryant|access-date=December 9, 2015|work=NBA.com|date=October 13, 2014}}</ref> The injury ruled him out of the first 25 games of the season, as he made his debut for the Bucks on December 17.<ref>{{cite news|last=Gruman|first=Andrew|title=Rookie O'Bryant could boost suddenly-thin Bucks frontcourt|url=http://www.foxsports.com/wisconsin/story/rookie-johnny-o-bryant-could-boost-suddenly-thin-milwaukee-bucks-frontcourt-121714|access-date=December 9, 2015|work=FoxSports.com|date=December 17, 2014}}</ref> On December 26, he scored a season-high 12 points in a 107–77 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Johnny O'Bryant 2014-15 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/obryajo01/gamelog/2015/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=April 18, 2015}}</ref>

On November 11, 2015, O'Bryant had a season-best game with 11 points and 9 rebounds in a loss to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Johnny O'Bryant 2015-16 Game Log|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/o/obryajo01/gamelog/2016/|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=December 9, 2015}}</ref>

On June 29, 2016, O'Bryant was waived by the Bucks.<ref>{{cite web|last=Gardner|first=Charles F.|url=http://www.jsonline.com/blogs/sports/384903521.html|title=Bucks waive Damien Inglis, Johnny O'Bryant|date=June 29, 2016|work=jsonline.com|access-date=July 2, 2016}}</ref>

On September 23, 2016, O'Bryant signed with the [[Washington Wizards]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|title=Wizards Finalize Training Camp Roster|work=Wizards Today|publisher=Monumental Sports Network|date=September 23, 2016|access-date=September 24, 2016|archive-date=March 30, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190330221751/https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/09/23/wizards-finalize-training-camp-roster|url-status=dead}}</ref> but was later waived on October 21 after appearing in four preseason games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://wizardstoday.monumentalsportsnetwork.com/2016/10/21/wizards-waive-three|title=Wizards Waive Three|work=Wizards Today|publisher=Monumental Sports Network|date=October 21, 2016|access-date=October 21, 2016}}</ref>

===Northern Arizona Suns (2016–2017)===
On November 11, 2016, O'Bryant was acquired by the [[Northern Arizona Suns]] of the [[NBA Development League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://northernarizona.dleague.nba.com/news/northern-arizona-suns-claim-johnny-obryant/|title=Northern Arizona Suns Claim Johnny O'Bryant|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 11, 2016|access-date=November 12, 2016|archive-date=November 12, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161112214527/http://northernarizona.dleague.nba.com/news/northern-arizona-suns-claim-johnny-obryant/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He made his debut for the Suns in the team's season opener the following day, recording 18 points and 12 rebounds in a 122–106 win over the [[Iowa Energy]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/games/20161112/iwanas/|title=Suns cruise past Energy to open inaugural season|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=November 12, 2016|access-date=November 13, 2016}}</ref> On January 16, 2017, he was named NBA Development League Performer of the Week for games played Monday, January 9 through Sunday, January 15.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dleague.nba.com/news/suns-johnny-obryant-nba-dleague-performer-of-week/|title=Suns' Johnny O'Bryant Named NBA D-League Performer of the Week|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 16, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2017}}</ref>

=== Denver Nuggets (2017) ===
On January 26, 2017, O'Bryant signed a 10-day contract with the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-johnny-obryant-10-day-contract-012517|title=Nuggets Sign Johnny O'Bryant to 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=January 26, 2017|access-date=January 26, 2017}}</ref> On February 6, 2017, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Nuggets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/nuggets-sign-obryant-10day-contract-020617|title=Nuggets Sign O'Bryant to Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 6, 2017|access-date=February 6, 2017}}</ref>

=== Return to Northern Arizona (2017) ===
O'Bryant returned to the Northern Arizona Suns on February 16 following the expiration of his second 10-day contract. Two days later, he participated in NBA D-League All-Star Game.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://northernarizona.dleague.nba.com/news/obryant-play-nba-d-league-star-game/|title=O'Bryant to Play in NBA D-League All-Star Game|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=February 17, 2017|access-date=February 22, 2017|archive-date=February 23, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170223125612/http://northernarizona.dleague.nba.com/news/obryant-play-nba-d-league-star-game/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

===Charlotte Hornets (2017–2018)===
On February 24, 2017, O'Bryant signed a 10-day contract with the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-forward-johnny-obryant-10-day-contract|title=Hornets Sign Forward Johnny O'Bryant To 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=February 24, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017}}</ref> On March 4, 2017, he scored a career-high 15 points in a 112–102 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900318|title=Walker scores 27 as Hornets beat Nuggets, 112-102|work=ESPN.com|date=March 4, 2017|access-date=March 5, 2017}}</ref> Two days later, he signed a second 10-day contract with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/obryant-signs-second-10-day-contract|title=O'Bryant Signs Second 10-Day Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 6, 2017|access-date=March 6, 2017}}</ref> On March 16, 2017, he signed a multi-year contract with the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/hornets-sign-johnny-obryant-multi-year-contract|title=Hornets Sign Johnny O'Bryant to Multi-Year Contract|work=NBA.com|date=March 16, 2017|access-date=March 16, 2017}}</ref>

On February 7, 2018, O'Bryant, along with two future second-round draft picks (2020 and 2021), was traded to the [[New York Knicks]] in exchange for [[Willy Hernangómez]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Knicks Acquire Two Second Round Draft Picks And Johnny O'Bryant From Charlotte|url=http://www.nba.com/knicks/knicks-acquire-two-second-round-draft-picks-and-johnny-obryant-charlotte|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 7, 2018|date=February 7, 2018}}</ref> He was waived by the Knicks the next day.<ref>{{cite web|author=NY_KnicksPR|url=https://twitter.com/ny_knickspr/status/961730398576242688|title=Knicks waive Johnny O'Bryant.|work=Twitter|date=February 8, 2018|access-date=February 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Maccabi Tel Aviv (2018–2019)===
[[File:Johnny O'Bryant 2019.jpg|thumb|O'Bryant with Maccabi Tel Aviv in March 2019]]
On July 31, 2018, O'Bryant signed a one-year deal with the Israeli team [[Maccabi Tel Aviv B.C.|Maccabi Tel Aviv]] of the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi signs newcomer O'Bryant at forward|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/8wrm3g6ejcyqb34r/maccabi-signs-newcomer-o-bryant-at-forward|work=EuroLeague.net|date=July 31, 2018|access-date=July 31, 2018}}</ref> On December 27, 2018, O'Bryant recorded a career-high 32 points, shooting 5-of-7 from 3-point range, along with five rebounds, three assists and three steals for 44 [[Performance Index Rating|PIR]], leading Maccabi to a 94–92 win over [[Pallacanestro Olimpia Milano|Olimpia Milano]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv vs. AX Armani Exchange Olimpia Milan|url=http://www.euroleague.net/main/results/showgame?gamecode=115&seasoncode=E2018|work=EuroLeague.net|date=December 27, 2018|access-date=December 28, 2018}}</ref> Two days later, he was named [[2018–19 EuroLeague#MVP of the Round|EuroLeague Round 15 MVP]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/9cwqbtkdn5ybsov4|title=Round 15 MVP: Johnny O'Bryant, Maccabi FOX Tel Aviv|date=October 29, 2018|work=EuroLeague.net|access-date=October 29, 2018}}</ref> O'Bryant went on to win the [[2019 Israeli Basketball Premier League Final Four|2019 Israeli League Championship]] with Maccabi.

===Lokomotiv Kuban (2019–2020)===
On August 14, 2019, O'Bryant signed with [[PBC Lokomotiv-Kuban|Lokomotiv Kuban]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Lokomotiv Kuban signs Johnny O'Bryant|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-johnny-obryant/|date=August 14, 2019|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=August 14, 2019|last1=Carchia|first1=Emiliano|archive-date=August 14, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190814132310/https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-signs-johnny-obryant/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He averaged 16.4 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 2.6 assists per game in VTB play. O'Bryant re-signed with the team on July 21, 2020.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lokomotiv Kuban officially re-signs Johnny O'Bryant |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-officially-re-signs-johnny-obryant/ |website=Sportando |access-date=July 21, 2020 |date=July 21, 2020|last1=Carchia |first1=Emiliano }}</ref> However, on September 18, he parted ways with the team due to a family issue.<ref>{{cite news |title=Lokomotiv Kuban, Johnny O'Bryant part ways |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/lokomotiv-kuban-johnny-obryant-part-ways/ |website=Sportando |access-date=September 18, 2020 |date=September 18, 2020|last1=Skerletic |first1=Dario }}</ref>

===Crvena zvezda (2020–2021)===
On October 19, 2020, O'Bryant signed with [[KK Crvena Zvezda|Crvena Zvezda]] of the [[ABA League|Adriatic League]] and the [[EuroLeague]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Johnny O'Bryant {{sic|offi|cialy|nolink=y}} joined Crvena zvezda |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/johnny-obryant-officialy-joined-crvena-zvezda/ |website=Sportando |access-date=October 19, 2020 |date=October 19, 2020|last1=Vezonik |first1=Uroš }}</ref> On January 27, 2021, he received a 10-day suspension from the club due to a conflict with team head coach [[Dejan Radonjić (basketball)|Dejan Radonjić]] during a game against [[Anadolu Efes S.K.|Anadolu Efes]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Radonjić: Niko nije iznad kluba, pa ni O'Brajant |url=https://www.mozzartsport.com/kosarka/vesti/radonjic-niko-nije-iznad-kluba-pa-ni-obrajant/377374 |website=mozzartsport.com |access-date=February 9, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=SK saznaje: O Brajant se sukobio sa Radonjićem, suspendovan |url=https://sportklub.rs/kosarka/sk-saznaje-o-brajant-se-sukobio-sa-radonjicem-suspendovan/ |website=sportklub.rs |date=January 29, 2021 |access-date=February 9, 2021}}</ref> On February 21, the Zvezda parted ways with O'Bryant.<ref>{{cite web |title=Rastanak Crvene zvezde i O'Brajanta |url=https://kkcrvenazvezda.rs/2021/02/21/rastanak-crvene-zvezde-i-obrajanta/ |website=kkcrvenazvezda.rs |date=February 21, 2021 |access-date=February 21, 2021}}</ref>

===Türk Telekom (2021)===
On February 21, 2021, O'Bryant signed with [[Türk Telekom B.K.|Türk Telekom]] of the [[Basketbol Süper Ligi|Turkish Basketball Super League]], for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title=Turk Telekom adds Johnny O'Bryant |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/fiba-champions-league/1172240/turk-telekom-adds-johnny-obryant/ |website=www.eurohoops.net/ |date=February 21, 2021 }}</ref>

On September 29, 2021, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] signed O'Bryant to a training camp deal.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Elijah Bryant and Johnny O'Bryant|url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-elijah-bryant-and-johnny-obryant|website=NBA.com|date=September 29, 2021|access-date=September 29, 2021}}</ref> He did not make the final roster however, and was waived on October 11.<ref>{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Bucks Cut Johnny O'Bryant|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/10/bucks-cut-johnny-obryant.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=October 11, 2021|access-date=October 31, 2021}}</ref>

===Wonju DB Promy (2021–2022)===
On November 15, 2021, O'Bryant signed with the [[Wonju DB Promy]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] to replace [[Yante Maten]] for eight weeks.<ref>{{cite web |title=프로농구 DB, 메이튼 대체로 NBA 출신 오브라이언트 영입 |url=https://yna.co.kr/view/AKR20211115047600007 |website=연합뉴스 |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=November 15, 2021}}</ref> On January 3, 2022, his contract was expired.<ref>{{cite web |title=[게임브리핑] 'NBA 도전' 오브라이언트 고별전, DB 당분간 외국선수 1명 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065606247033133 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=January 3, 2022}}</ref> On January 5, he re-signed with the Wonju DB Promy for the remainder of the season.<ref>{{cite web |title='시즌 대체 확정' DB, 오브라이언트와 계약 연장 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065605772437921 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=January 6, 2022}}</ref>

===Meralco Bolts (2022)===
On August 6, 2022, he signed with the [[Meralco Bolts]] of the [[Philippine Basketball Association]] (PBA) as the team's import for the [[2022–23 PBA Commissioner's Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://mb.com.ph/2022/08/06/meralco-taps-former-nba-player-johnny-obryant-as-comms-cup-import/|title=Meralco taps former NBA player Johnny O'Bryant as Comm's Cup import|website=[[Manila Bulletin]]|date=August 6, 2022|accessdate=August 10, 2022}}</ref> He was set to be replaced by [[Jessie Govan]] after a 1–5 start to the conference,<ref>{{cite web|last=Terrado|first=Reuben|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/jessie-govan-replaces-johnny-o-bryant-as-meralco-import-a795-20221025 |title=Jessie Govan tapped to replace O'Bryant, revive Meralco playoff hopes|website=spin.ph|date=October 25, 2022|accessdate=October 28, 2022}}</ref> but O'Bryant stayed with the team when Govan was measured above the conference's 6'10" height limit.<ref>{{cite web|last=Ramos|first=Gerry|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/meralco-to-play-o-bryant-as-replacement-over-height-limit-a793-20221028 |title=Meralco stuck with O'Bryant as replacement 'over the height limit' |website=spin.ph|date=October 28, 2022|accessdate=October 28, 2022}}</ref> He was supposed to play another game on October 30, but the game was postponed due to [[Tropical Storm Nalgae (2022)|Tropical Storm Paeng]].<ref>{{cite news|last=Terrado|first=Ruben|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/pba-games-cancelled-due-to-typhoon-paeng-a795-20221029|title=PBA games cancelled as Typhoon Paeng brings strong wind, rain|website=Sports Interactive Network Philippines|date=October 29, 2022|accessdate=October 31, 2022}}</ref> On October 31, he was finally replaced by [[K. J. McDaniels]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Terrado|first=Reuben|url=https://www.spin.ph/basketball/pba/meralco-taps-ex-nlex-import-kj-mcdaniels-for-johnny-o-bryant-a795-20221031 |title=Meralco bringing in former NLEX import KJ McDaniels as O'Bryant replacement|website=spin.ph|date=October 31, 2022|accessdate=October 31, 2022}}</ref>

===Shanghai Sharks (2022–2023)===
In October 2022, O'Bryant signed with the [[Shanghai Sharks]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=Johnny O'Bryant joins Shanghai Sharks|url=https://sportando.basketball/en/johnny-obryant-joins-shanghai-sharks/|date=October 24, 2022|newspaper=Sportando|access-date=February 20, 2023|last=Carchia |first=Emiliano }}</ref>

===Ibaraki Robots (2023–2024)===
On November 15, 2023, O'Bryant signed with the [[Ibaraki Robots]] of the [[B.League]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=#84 ジョニー・オブライアント選手 契約合意(新規)のご報告|url=https://www.ibarakirobots.win/news/20231115_08_team/|publisher=Ibaraki Robots|language=ja|date=November 15, 2023|access-date=November 15, 2023}}</ref> On April 9, 2024, his contract was terminated.<ref>{{cite web |title=#84 ジョニー・オブライアント選手 退団のお知らせ |url=https://www.ibarakirobots.win/news/20240409_01_team/ |website=茨城ロボッツ |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=April 9, 2024}}</ref>

===Gigantes de Carolina (2024)===
On July 12, 2024, O'Bryant signed with the [[Gigantes de Carolina (men's basketball)|Gigantes de Carolina]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{cite web |title=Carolina inks Johnny O'Bryant III, ex Ibaraki R. |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Japan/news/881345/Carolina-inks-Johnny-OBryant-III-ex-Ibaraki-R |website=Eurobasket.com |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=July 12, 2024}}</ref>

===Uralmash Yekaterinburg (2024–2025)===
On September 23, 2024, O'Bryant signed with the [[BC Uralmash Yekaterinburg|Uralmash Yekaterinburg]] of the [[VTB United League]].<ref>{{cite web |title=ДЖОННИ О'БРАЙАНТ III — НОВЫЙ ИГРОК БК «УРАЛМАШ» |url=https://bcuralmash.ru/news/dzhonni-obrajant-iii-novyj-igrok-bk-uralmash/ |website=БК Уралмаш |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=September 23, 2024}}</ref> On January 9, 2025, Uralmash Yekaterinburg parted ways with O'Bryant.<ref>{{cite web |title=СПАСИБО ЗА ИГРУ, ДЖОННИ! |url=https://bcuralmash.ru/news/spasibo-za-igru-dzhonni/ |website=БК Уралмаш |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=January 9, 2025}}</ref>

===Anyang Jung Kwan Jang Red Boosters (2025)===
On January 13, 2025, O'Bryant signed with the [[Anyang Jung Kwan Jang Red Boosters]] of the [[Korean Basketball League]] (KBL) to replace [[Cliff Alexander]].<ref>{{cite web |title='반등 위한 마지막 승부수' 정관장, 새 외국선수로 전 DB 오브라이언트 영입···알렉산더 퇴출 |url=https://jumpball.co.kr/news/newsview.php?ncode=1065574180859118 |website=점프볼 |access-date=January 13, 2025 |date=January 13, 2025}}</ref>

=== Sagesse SC (basketball) (2025-present) ===
On April 18, 2025, O'Bryant signed with the [[Sagesse SC (basketball)|Sagesse SC]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sagesse adds O'Bryant III to their roster, ex Anyang |url=https://www.asia-basket.com/Lebanon/news/929438/Sagesse-adds-OBryant-III-to-their-roster-ex-Anyang |access-date=2025-11-20 |website=www.asia-basket.com}}</ref>.

==Business career==
O'Bryant founded the anime and manga publisher Noir Caesar in 2017. The company signed a deal with [[Tokyopop]] in 2023.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://bleedingcool.com/comics/johnny-lee-obryant-iii-signs-noir-caesar-manga-deal-through-tokyopop/ | title=Johnny Lee O'Bryant III Signs Noir Caesar Manga Deal Through Tokyopop | date=March 2023 }}</ref>
